samples.summary: New "PUSH LAST / nothing after the push" rule contradicts the surviving post-push verification instruction
samples.evidence: The diff adds at 1729-1734: "PUSH LAST ... the push is the end of your turn, not the middle of it ... anything you try to do afterwards is racing a cancellation you triggered yourself". But lines 1750-1754 (unchanged) still require post-push work: "Then CONFIRM the push landed with `git ls-remote origin <branch>` rather than trusting the exit code ... If the remote head did not advance, push again before your turn ends." Those two instructions cannot both be obeyed: the confirm/re-push step is by definition after the push and inside the ~30s cancellation window the new text tells the agent to treat as unusable. A fixer that takes "PUSH LAST" literally drops the ls-remote confirmation that exists to catch a push whose hook output made it report non-zero while the ref did not advance — the exact failure mode that ends in the "Page if the fix produced no commit" dead-end at line 1806. The prompt should say explicitly that the ls-remote confirmation (and only that) is the one permitted post-push action.

samples.summary: Prompt now tells the fixer to report "AFTER COMMITTING" but the commit instruction appears ~60 lines later in the prompt
samples.evidence: Line 1665 states "REPORT WHAT YOU DID — AFTER COMMITTING, BEFORE PUSHING", and the report command block follows immediately (1683). The instruction to actually create the commit is only given at line 1725 ("Append a follow-up commit (do NOT force-push); the commit message must end with the trailer ..."), i.e. after the report block and after the rebuttal block. An agent reading the prompt in order can post the report before any commit exists, at which point the report's `file:line` notes describe uncommitted work and the required trailer/commit step is reached last. The stated sequence (commit → report → push) is not the sequence the prompt presents; the commit paragraph should be moved above the report section so document order matches the load-bearing order the change is about.

samples.summary: Ordering test slices the "prompt" to end-of-file, so its assertions can be satisfied by text belonging to a different job
samples.evidence: `const prompt = wf.slice(wf.indexOf("The review panel requested changes on your PR."))` takes everything from line 1642 to EOF (the file continues with close-stuck-checks/stalled jobs at 1915/1978). `report`, `push` and `rebuttal` are then first-occurrence indices anywhere in that tail. If the fixer prompt later loses its push instruction (or its report block) while some later section of the workflow contains a matching string, `report < push` and the doesNotMatch guard still pass while the invariant under test is broken. Bounding the slice to the end of the fixer prompt (e.g. up to the `claude_args:`/`--max-turns` marker at 1767) would make the test measure the region it claims to measure.

samples.summary: Report-before-push allows a "fixed" report to exist on the PR with no corresponding pushed commit
samples.evidence: With the new ordering the fix report is posted before the push, so a run whose push fails, is denied, or exhausts the turn budget after the report leaves a report claiming `--fixed` for code that never reached the remote. `authorClaims`/`latestReport` (scripts/agent/fix-report.mjs:233-285) treat the latest report as the authoritative claim set for the next round and feed the fixed claims to the adjudicator, and fix-brief renders skipped/fixed notes back to the next fixer. The adjudicator upholds by default when it re-reads the code, so this is not a soundness hole, but the report is now a claim about a tree the remote never saw, and `--head` is still the pre-fix `workflow_run.head_sha` so nothing downstream can detect the mismatch. Worth a note in the prompt (or a head check) that a report without a landed push is expected to be superseded.

samples.summary: The sibling on-demand fixer prompt still uses the old "THEN REPORT / push" wording and is not covered by the new ordering test
samples.evidence: agent-fix.yml:333-394 keeps "THEN REPORT WHAT YOU DID" with the push described afterwards and no ordering statement. Its own concurrency (agent-fix.yml:78-80) is `cancel-in-progress: false` and it is not in the panel's concurrency group, so the specific #757 race does not apply there — but the two prompts have now diverged, and the new test only inspects agent-review-panel.yml, so nothing keeps them consistent.
